questions.question_text: A shopkeeper sells 2 Kg of rice to Latha and 3 Kg of rice to Lalitha. To Latha, he marks up the price by 8% and also underweighs the quantity of rice by 10%. For Lalitha, he sells the rice at the cost price, but underweighs the quantity of rice by 20%. What is his overall profit percentage?
questions.solution_text:
Let the cost price of the rice be Rs. 100 per Kg.
As he sold a total of 5 Kg, his total cost price is Rs. 500
To Latha, the selling price is Rs. 108 per Kg.
As he underweighs the quantity of rice by 10%, the apparent quantity of rice sold to Latha is 2/0.9 = 2.22 Kg
The total money he received from Latha is 108*2.22 = Rs. 240
To Lalitha, the selling price is Rs. 100 per Kg.
As he underweighs the quantity of rice by 20%, the apparent quantity of rice sold to Lalitha is 3/0.8 = 3.75 Kg
The total money he received from Lalitha is 100*3.75 = Rs. 375
The total money he received 240+375 = Rs. 615
Hence, his overall profit percentage is 615/500-1 = 23%

questions.question_text: A large cube is cut into n smaller cubes such that all n cubes have equal dimensions and no part of the larger cube remains. If the surface area increases by 4 times, what is the value of n?
questions.solution_text:
Since all the cubes are of the same dimensions, let us say that we are forming cubes that have half the length of the original cube. In that case, we need to have three mutually perpendicular cuts parallel to the faces of the cube.
In this case, the surface area becomes twice. because we are introducing one more set of surfaces.
Similarly, when we cut this into a cube such that the side of the smaller cubes is one-fifth of the side of the older cube, we increase the surface area by 4 times, or to five times, and we get 125 cubes.

questions.question_text: The average age of a family is 25 years. If two people of an average age of 30 replace the youngest member of the family, the average age of the family is increased by 4. If the eldest member, whose age is 45 years, of the family, leaves the group, the average age decreases by 4. Find the average age of the current family when the youngest member was born.
questions.solution_text:
Initial average = 25 years
Elder member's age = 45 years
Since average age decreases by 4,
The new average = 21 years
Let the total members in the family is x.
New Average = $\frac{\left(25x-45\right)}{\left(x-1\right)}$
$21=\frac{\left(25x-45\right)}{\left(x-1\right)}$
$25x-45=21x-21$
x = 6
Let the age of youngest member is y.
Since average age increases by 4,
Thus, new average = 29 years
Total family members = 7
New average = $\frac{\left(25\times\ 6+60-y\right)}{7}$
$29=\frac{\left(150+60-y\right)}{7}$
$203=210-y$
y = 7 years.
Thus, y was born 7 years before.
Since average age have to be found when y was born,
Total family members = 6
$Average\ age=\frac{\left(150-7\times\ 6\right)}{6}$
= $(25-7)$
= 18 years.

questions.question_text: The average speed of HYD VSKP DT Express is 60 kmph, if the halts at various stations is excluded then the average speed is 80kmph. What is the average halt time per hour of DT express?

In one hour, DT express covers 80 km.
When the halt time is included, then the express covers 60 km
Because of the halts, the train lost covering 20 km
In hour the train stops for 60*$\frac{20}{80}$ = 15 minutes

questions.question_text: Ten men and eight women working for 12 days can complete a piece of work which can be completed by twelve men working for 16 days. If eight men and six women are currently working, the number of additional women required to complete the work in 9.6 days is
questions.solution_text:
Consider the work done by 1 man in 1 day = M units and that by a woman in 1 day = W units
Hence, (10M + 8W)*12 = 12M*16
120 M + 96W = 192M
96W = 72M 
4W = 3M
Total work = 12M *16 = 192M
Let x be the number of additional women to be employed.
(8M + 6W+xW)9.6 = 192 M
(8M + 6*$\frac{3M}{4}$+x*$\frac{3M}{4}$)9.6 = 192 M
(8M + $\frac{18M}{4}$+$\frac{3xM}{4}$)9.6 = 192 M
($\frac{50}{4}$+$\frac{3x}{4}$) =20
x = 10
10 is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: A faulty machine records the price and number of goods purchased but reverses the digits of the number of goods when computing the bill. In one of the billings, the number of goods recorded was 63 less than the actual number of goods sold and the total value of the goods sold was Rs.696. What is the actual price of one such goods? (Each goods is of same value and price is a whole number)
questions.solution_text:
Let the faulty value of the number of goods be ab
Let actual value of number of goods be ba.
ba-ab=63
10*b+a-(10*a+b)=63
9(b-a)=63
b-a=7
So we have the following possibilities (9,2),(8,1),(7,0)
So the possible values of cost of each article are 92,29,18,81,7,70
Among the above values only 29 divides 696.(Since the price is a whole number)
So the number of goods as shown by the faulty machine=29
Price of each good=$\frac{696}{29}$
=24
A is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Raju invested a sum of money at 20% compound interest. He invested an equal amount of money at 20% simple interest. In how many years will the amount become at least double of the principal?
questions.solution_text:
Let the total principal be 2P.
So, principal invested at 20% compound interest = P
Principal invested at 20% simple interest = P
Let the amount double in ‘n’ years
So, $P(1+20/100)^n + P + P*n*20/100 = 4P$
=> $(1.2)^n + 1 + 0.2n = 4$
=> $(1.2)^n + 0.2n = 3$
=> From the options, we see that n = 5 satisfies the required condition

questions.question_text: 12 workers (4 men, 4 women, 4 boys) work on a project. The efficiency of no two workers is the same. A group consists of 1 man, 1 woman and  1 boy. The project was completed when all the distinct groups possible worked for exactly one day each. What portion of the work can be completed in one day if all the workers work together?
questions.solution_text:
There are 12 workers (4 men, 4 women, 4 boys)
The number of ways i.e groups in which they can work is 4*4*4 = 64
Number of distinct groups = 64
Every worker will work in 16 groups.
Let the total work = $W$ units
16$(M_1+M_2+M_3+M_4 + W_1+W_2+W_3+W_4 + B_1+B_2+B_3+B_4)$ = $W$
$(M_1+M_2+M_3+M_4 + W_1+W_2+W_3+W_4 + B_1+B_2+B_3+B_4)$= $\frac{W}{16}$
So the portion of work done by 12 workers in one day= $\frac{\frac{W}{16}}{W}$
= 1:16
D is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Three unbiased dice are rolled simultaneously. What is the probability the sum of the numbers obtained on the three dice is at least 16?
questions.solution_text:
When three dice are rolled, the maximum sum that can be obtained is 18.
So, in the given question, the sum can be 16 or 17 or 18
For the sum to be 16, there can be two possibilities:
1. (6 , 6 , 4) - total cases = $\frac{3!}{2!}$ = 3
2. (6, 5, 5) - total cases = $\frac{3!}{2!}$ = 3
For the sum to be 17, there can be only one possibility:
1. (6, 6, 5) - total cases = $\frac{3!}{2!}$ = 3
For the sum to be 18, there is only one case which is (6, 6, 6)
So, the no. of favourable outcomes = (3 + 3 + 3 + 1) = 10
Total no. of outcomes = 6 * 6 * 6 = 216
Required probability = $\frac{10}{216}$ = $\frac{5}{108}$
Hence, option D is the correct answer.

The runners A and C with speed in ratio 1:3 will intersect at 3-1 =2 points. 
The runners A and D with speed in ratio 1:5 will intersect at 5-1 =4 points. 
The runners B and C with speed in ratio 2:3 will intersect at 3-2 =1 points. 
The runners B and D with speed in ratio 2:5 will intersect at 5-2 =3 points. 
The runners C and D with speed in ratio 3:5 will intersect at 5-2 =2 points. 
The points will coincide for runners A,B; A,C; B,C ;C,D and A,D with each other as they are start the race from the same point.
Number of different points at which they will intersect is given in the figure below.
They will intersect at 6 different points.

questions.question_text: In a class, a test was conducted and out of passed students, 60% were girls. 20% of the total boys failed. Find the pass percentage among the girls if the ratio of the number of boys to girls is 5:8.
questions.solution_text:
Assuming the total number of students is 130, then the number of boys = 50 and the number of girls = 80
Total number of boys who failed =20% of 50 =  10, then the number of boys who passed = 40
Out of total passed students, 60%, were girls. Hence 40% would be the boys = 40% of the passed students = 40
=> Total number of passed students = 100
=> The number of girls who passed = 60
The pass percentage of girls = $\dfrac{60}{80}\times\ 100$ = 75

When x=9, (x-6)(x-8)(x-10)...............(x-88) > 0
When x=11, (x-6)(x-8)(x-10)...............(x-88) < 0
So x = 7, 11, 15,.....87, (x-6)(x-8)(x-10)...............(x-88) < 0
Number of values of x 
87=7+(n-1)4
n=21
Sum of an A.P= $\frac{n}{2}$*[2a+(n-1)d] where n is the number of terms,a= first term, d= common difference
Here a=7, n=21, d=4
Sum of all the values of x =$\frac{21}{2}$*[2*7+(21-1)4]
=987
B is the correct answer.

The critical points or the values of x for which the (x-6)(x-8)(x-10)...............(x-88) is 0 is 6, 8, 10, ........88
Number of values =
88=6+(n-1)2
n=42
There are 42 terms, If odd number of terms are negative then (x-6)(x-8)(x-10)...............(x-88) < 0
For all the negative integers, (x-6)(x-8)(x-10)...............(x-88) > 0

When x=7, (x-6)(x-8)(x-10)...............(x-88) < 0
When x=9, (x-6)(x-8)(x-10)...............(x-88) > 0

So x = 7, 11, 15,.....87, (x-6)(x-8)(x-10)...............(x-88) < 0
Number of values of x 
87=7+(n-1)4
n=21
Sum of an A.P= $\frac{n}{2}$*[2a+(n-1)d] where n is the number of terms,a= first term, d= common difference
Here a=7, n=21, d=4
Sum of all the values of x =$\frac{21}{2}$*[2*7+(21-1)4]
=987
B is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: A container has 50 litres of ethanol. Using a mug of volume 'X' litres of the solution is removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated three times using the same mug and after that, only 25.6 litres of ethanol is left in the container. What is the volume of the mug?
questions.solution_text:
We can use the formula
Quantity left = Quantity present initially * $(1-\frac{\text{Quantity removed}}{\text{Total Quantity}})^n$
where n is the number of iteration.
Let the quantity removed in each iteration be x litres
Putting all values we get 
25.6 = 50 * $(1-\frac{x}{50})^3$
Solving this equation we can get x=10 litres
Hence, option B is correct.

questions.question_text: $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of the equation $3x^{2} + 9x + p = 0$. If $\frac{1}{\alpha^{2} } + \frac{1}{\beta^{2} } > 1$, then what is a possible value of p
questions.solution_text:
$\alpha + \beta = -3$ and $\alpha \beta = p/3$
$\frac{1}{\alpha^{2} } + \frac{1}{\beta^{2} } = \frac{\alpha ^{2} + \beta ^{2}}{(\alpha \beta )^{2}}=\frac{(\alpha + \beta )^{2} - 2\alpha \beta }{(\alpha \beta)^{2}} > 1$
substituting $\alpha + \beta$ and $\alpha \beta$ we get,
$p^{2} + 6p -81 < 0$
a = 6 is the only possible value from the options that satisfies the above inequality.Thus option B is the correct choice.

questions.question_text: S is the sum of 120 consecutive natural numbers. If 'n' is the smallest number of the series and S is a perfect square, what will be be the minimum value of the last number of the series?
questions.solution_text:
The first term =n,  The last term = n+119
Now the sum of the numbers= S = [n/2][first term+last term] = [120/2][n+n+119] 
=> S=60[2n+119] = 4*15[2n+119]
S will be a square when [2n+119] is equal to 15k where k is a square,
2n+119=15k
The minimum value of k can be 9, hence 2n+119=15*9 =135   =>2n=16  =>n=8
Then the last term = n+119=8+119=127

questions.question_text: A triangle ABC of perimeter 70 cm is circumscribed by a circle of radius 15 cm such that AB is the diameter. Find the area of the triangle(in cm$^2$).
questions.solution_text:
Consider the following figure:
ACB will be a right angle. (Angle in the semicircle)
Now, AB+BC+AC=70
Now, AB = 15*2 = 30 cm
=> BC+AC = 70-30 = 40 cm ......(1)
Also, $BC^2+AC^2=30^2$  (Using pythagoras) ......(2)
Squaring the first equation and subtracting the second equation from it, we get
2BC*AC = 40*40-30*30 = 700  .....(3)
Area of triangle ACB = $\frac{1}{2}\times\ BC\times\ AC$ = 700/4 = 175 cm$^2$ (dividing equation 3 by 4)

questions.question_text: In how many ways can 10 children be seated in 10 seats from left to the right such that 2 particular children are never together?
questions.solution_text:
Number of ways in which the 2 particular children are not together = Total number of ways - Number of ways in which they are together
Total number of ways = 10!
Number of ways in which 2 particular children are together = (10-1)!.2!=9!2!
Hence, the number of ways in which the 2 particular children are never together = $10!-9!2!=9!\left(10-2\right)=9!.8$
